The *Kaṇhajātaka* (Ja 29), translated into English as *The Bull Named Black*, is a short tale preserved in the Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to the narrative framework preserved in its blurb, the Buddha recounted this past-life story while staying at the Jetavana monastery in connection with the Double Miracle, an episode noted as being treated alongside the Descent from Heaven in the thirteenth book's *Sarabhamigajātaka*. The core verse opens with the phrase "With heavy loads".
